newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks fall 1.39 percent by lunch break.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks fall 1.39 percent by lunch break.

text.p: Squeezed by tight liquidity in the money market, investors sold stocks on Tuesday morning and drove the index down 1.39 percent in thin trade by the lunch break, brokers said.

"Liquidity in the money market was quite tight this morning. Investors also wanted to wait for more half-year earnings results of banks and finance companies," said Witawus Charuchandr of Ekachart Finance and Securities.
The composite SET index declined 9.08 points to 644.29 on 2.5 billion baht turnover by the break.

There was a higher demand for cash on Tuesday, which is the deadline for commercial banks to meet their twice-monthly reserve requirements. The overnight interbank rate rose to 16-18 percent early from 14-15 percent on Friday.
Half-year earnings of banks and finance companies began trickling in and most of them were poor as anticipated by investors, brokers said.
Most of the key sectors declined by the break. The finance sector gained most in terms of value, rising 2.58 percent.
National Finance topped the active list, gaining 0.75 baht to 38.75. -- Suthep Chawla (662) 652-0642
